_comment: Graphics presets applied by the Settings > Graphics buttons (native; the web settings page mirrors the list). 'ultra' is THE REFERENCE: what the probe rig measures and what 'Ultra' means in every performance number in docs/PRIORITIES.md, so an operator on this preset sees what the rig sees. 'extreme' pushes every slider to its limit (full-resolution cloud march, triple grass, exaggerated air and occlusion) and is for finding the ceiling, not for play. Keys are SettingsState field names (src/gui/mod.rs) plus cloud_res_div (GuiState, persisted by config cloud_res_div). Unknown keys are logged and ignored so this file can grow ahead of the code.

presets.name: Ultra (reference)
presets.note: The rig's reference: cloud march at half resolution, constructed cloud bodies, every surface and lighting feature on at its physical strength.

presets.name: Extreme (every slider at its limit)
presets.note: Above the reference: the cloud march at full resolution (4x the reference cost), triple grass, air and occlusion past their physical strength. For finding the ceiling.

presets.name: Minimum (rigs only)
presets.note: NOT listed in Settings. The graphics the verification rigs run at while the operator uses his PC (2026-10-22, HUMANITY_LOW_IMPACT, src/engine/low_impact.rs; which rigs and when: scripts/lib/rig-needs.js): laid over the sandbox config and never saved. Drawing only: clouds off, bounced light at its Ambient level, sun shadows, god rays, ambient occlusion, grass and the night-sky extras off, rain at its least, few 3D tree models. It never names a setting that changes what the game does: the water waves (water_fft is the float), the trees that stand (tree_density), the rain path (gpu_particles off moves rain to the processor), the terrain shape or streaming, the weather. Keys are config.json names; src/engine/low_impact.rs tests that each one is.
